sections.heading: 1. Kill fabricated earnings before they become leveraged purchase price
paragraphs: Start with the first mapped play, QoE normalization, rather than the broker's adjusted earnings headline. The fatal traps are treating seller discretionary earnings as transferable cash flow, accepting recurring expenses as one-time addbacks, and capitalizing revenue that has not survived collection. Obtain twenty-four months of QuickBooks Online or Xero general ledgers, bank statements, Stripe settlement exports, payroll registers, and filed tax returns. Tie monthly invoices to deposits through a bridge separating sales tax, refunds, processor fees, customer deposits, and receivable timing. A deposit is not automatically revenue, and a tax return is corroborating evidence rather than a substitute for transaction testing. Replace the seller's labor with a priced role before accepting an owner-compensation addback. Illustratively, $300,000 of claimed earnings less a $90,000 replacement manager, $20,000 recurring repairs, and $15,000 unsupported revenue leaves $175,000. At four times earnings, the difference creates $500,000 of purchase-price exposure. Those figures describe a diligence example, not an alternative scorecard. Require a document-backed explanation for every adjustment above $5,000 and investigate any unexplained monthly collection bridge exceeding 1% of sales. These are buyer-selected investigation thresholds, not accounting standards. If the seller cannot resolve the bridge, remove the adjustment and reprice instead of stretching leverage to preserve the original bid.

The second mapped play, working-capital protection, prevents a profitable acquisition from arriving without the cash resources required to operate. Define the delivered working-capital calculation in the purchase agreement using named general-ledger accounts, consistent accounting policies, and sample calculations. Specify treatment of accrued payroll, inventory reserves, customer deposits, deferred revenue, sales taxes, and debt-like items; classification disputes can otherwise count the same obligation twice. Use a seasonally representative monthly average rather than a convenient year-end snapshot. Suppose the agreed target is $180,000 and the final delivered amount is $145,000: the $35,000 shortfall requires the agreed price adjustment, not a vague promise of future collections. Test receivables against subsequent cash receipts, credit memos, disputes, and customer acceptance records. Inventory needs physical counts and aging by SKU; a $40,000 obsolete stock reserve can consume much of the Conservative case's $60,000 annual profit. For prepaid service contracts, model the remaining fulfillment cost separately from the accounting liability so liquidity planning does not confuse those measures. Escalate when receivable days increase ten days above the comparable seasonal baseline or overdue balances exceed the negotiated reserve assumptions. The fallback is a larger funded adjustment reserve, a reduced price, or withdrawal before signing an economically unworkable settlement mechanism.

The third mapped play is debt-service structuring, where newcomers confuse accounting profit with distributable cash. The canonical Conservative case has $750,000 sales, an 8% margin, and $60,000 owner profit; Base has $1,875,000, 13.0%, and $243,750; Scaled has $3,000,000, 18%, and $540,000. Each margin is after interest and before principal repayments. Conservative and Base each require seven full-time staff plus three contractors; Scaled requires eight plus four. Illustratively, subtracting $120,000 annual principal and $30,000 maintenance capital spending from Base profit leaves $93,750 before additional working-capital needs and owner-level taxes. Do not deduct interest again in that cash bridge. Separately calculate the lender's contractual debt-service coverage ratio using its defined cash-flow numerator and required principal-plus-interest denominator. If that numerator is $300,000 and scheduled service is $240,000, coverage is 1.25 times; a $60,000 cash-flow reduction consumes the entire cushion. Treat that ratio as an example, not a universal SBA covenant. Obtain written confirmation of seller-note payment restrictions, standby treatment, guarantees, collateral, and reporting obligations. Stress variable interest, seasonal borrowing, and covenant headroom together. If the business cannot fund operations and contractual service without hoped-for refinancing, reduce debt, negotiate permitted contingent consideration, inject committed equity, or stop the transaction.

callout.title: Buy the evidence trail before buying the earnings story
callout.body: Experienced buyers make disputed economics testable while they still possess negotiating leverage.
items: Sample the largest invoices plus random smaller invoices; trace each through delivery evidence, customer acceptance, settlement, and subsequent credit memos.
Have both transaction accountants calculate a mock working-capital settlement before signing, then resolve policy differences in a worked contractual exhibit.
Price seller duties from a two-week activity log and customer escalation history rather than relying on the seller's estimated weekly workload.
Maintain separate lender-coverage and owner-cash bridges so interest, principal, capital spending, and seller-note restrictions cannot disappear through presentation choices.

sections.heading: 2. Contain inherited liabilities, seller clawbacks and unlawful shortcuts
paragraphs: The fourth mapped play, liability containment, starts by rejecting the assumption that an asset purchase erases the past. Entity purchases ordinarily retain entity obligations, while asset transactions can still encounter statutory successor rules, assumed contracts, liens, and fact-specific successor liability. Build a liability register covering payroll, overtime, worker classification, sales taxes, environmental conditions, permits, employee benefits, litigation, and customer warranties. Use 29 U.S.C. 207 to test covered nonexempt overtime rather than accepting a salaried job title as the answer. A rough screening example of ten employees, five unpaid overtime hours weekly, and a $30 overtime rate produces $78,000 across fifty-two weeks before other amounts; actual exposure depends on pay already received, coverage, exemptions, and the applicable recovery period. Flag every contractor performing an employee-like core role for jurisdiction-specific review. California Revenue and Taxation Code section 6811 illustrates why a purchaser may need to withhold purchase money pending the specified sales-tax evidence. Resolve applicable clearance procedures before releasing seller proceeds. A seller indemnity is only as useful as its scope, survival, exclusions, and collectibility. For material unresolved exposure, require a funded escrow, an effective price adjustment, or a transaction structure that actually addresses the identified obligation rather than merely renaming it.

Hidden clawbacks also arise from settlement mechanics, indemnity baskets, insurance exclusions, and creditor challenges. A $25,000 deductible basket can leave the buyer bearing the first $25,000 of otherwise covered losses; a tipping basket works differently, so read the actual clause. Caps, survival periods, exclusive remedies, knowledge qualifiers, and claim-notice deadlines can turn a persuasive claim into an unrecoverable expense. Create a calendar that starts at closing and records the required recipient, delivery method, supporting evidence, and deadline for each claim category. Separately search UCC filings in the relevant debtor jurisdictions, confirm debtor identity, and obtain payoff letters covering the assets being acquired. A filing search alone does not establish every lien or release obligation. UCC section 9-315 generally preserves a security interest after disposition unless an applicable exception or secured-party authorization applies. Bankruptcy adds another asymmetry: 11 U.S.C. 547 can permit avoidance of qualifying preferential transfers, commonly within ninety days and potentially one year for insiders; section 548 addresses specified fraudulent transfers within two years. Other applicable law can reach different periods. Neither provision automatically invalidates an ordinary acquisition. Nevertheless, distressed-seller deals need solvency analysis, defensible valuation, properly sequenced payoffs, and specialist review before funds move; a cheap price cannot cure defective title.

The fifth mapped play, customer retention, exposes two further traps: buying relationships that belong to the departing seller and treating contracts as freely transferable. Rank customers by collected gross profit, renewal date, change-of-control language, concentration, and operational dependence on named personnel. With seller authorization, conduct structured customer calls that test service continuity without announcing unsupported commitments. If one customer supplies $375,000 of Base sales at a 30% contribution margin, losing that account removes $112,500 of contribution before avoidable overhead adjustments. That is roughly 46% of the $243,750 Base owner-profit case, not merely a 20% revenue inconvenience. Use signed transition responsibilities, permitted retention-linked consideration, and key-person coverage rather than optimistic statements about loyalty. For government work, distinguish asset transfers from stock transactions and evaluate FAR 42.1204 novation requirements against the actual structure. Never backdate customer approvals, fabricate lender invoices, misstate equity sources, or conceal beneficial ownership to rescue a timetable. Such shortcuts create fraud exposure and can also terminate financing or commercial relationships. Mark every critical assignment, permit transfer, and lender representation as an evidence requirement with a responsible owner. If a material contract cannot continue lawfully on the proposed structure, exclude its earnings from valuation or defer closing until a workable documented arrangement exists.

Plausible losses exceed funded recovery or expire before reliable detection.
Negotiate targeted escrow and specific protection instead of relying on labels.
Trap 11: Existing security interests survive the buyer's asset transfer.
Match debtor searches with collateral schedules, payoff letters, and release instructions.
A secured party has not authorized the required collateral release.
Coordinate payment and release through a documented closing funds sequence.
Trap 12: Concentrated customer contracts cannot survive the planned ownership change.
Read assignment clauses and obtain authorized customer or contracting-officer responses.
A material account lacks a lawful and documented continuation path.
Remove exposed earnings from valuation or postpone the affected transaction.

sections.heading: 3. Detect platform restrictions and margin leaks before liquidity fails
paragraphs: The sixth mapped play, payment-platform continuity, matters whenever an acquired merchant depends on Stripe, PayPal, Amazon, Shopify Payments, or another intermediary. A business acquisition does not automatically transfer the right to use an account, its underwriting history, or its existing settlement terms. Review the specific provider agreement and obtain its ownership-change process before promising uninterrupted collections. Do not buy aged accounts, falsify beneficial-owner records, manufacture reviews, route prohibited transactions through another merchant category, or open concealed replacement accounts after restrictions. Those shortcuts can produce lasting account termination, frozen settlements, and contractual or legal exposure. Inventory authorized administrators, multifactor authentication devices, domains, bank destinations, API credentials, refund rights, and customer data permissions. Transfer access through approved mechanisms and rotate credentials without interrupting legitimate fulfillment. A processor holding 10% of $100,000 monthly card volume withholds $10,000 that month; three months without releases traps $30,000 before considering subsequent releases or additional reserves. That reserve is a liquidity restriction, not automatically an operating expense. Chargeback losses and fees have different accounting effects. If continuity remains uncertain, secure provider-approved onboarding and a lawful alternative collection rail such as customer-authorized ACH invoicing; never represent another merchant's credentials as an operational backup. Delay closing when no usable settlement path exists.

Build telemetry from the acquired company's actual transaction grain, not a dashboard assembled from unrelated monthly totals. Join orders, invoices, shipments, labor time, refunds, disputes, and settlements through stable identifiers. A PostgreSQL database with Metabase reporting can expose contribution by customer and SKU while retaining drill-through evidence; a controlled spreadsheet is adequate for smaller datasets if reconciled and versioned. Calculate realized contribution as recognized sales less the directly attributable costs defined in the operating model, including fulfillment, payment charges, refunds, and variable labor where applicable. Do not call that measure net margin because overhead and financing remain elsewhere. At Base sales, one percentage point of net-margin erosion equals $18,750 annually; three points equal $56,250, or about 23% of canonical owner profit. Investigate a two-percentage-point contribution decline against a comparable four-week baseline, separating mix changes from price leakage and labor overruns. Illustratively, $20,000 monthly card volume at 2.9% plus thirty cents across four hundred transactions costs $700 before other charges. A quote showing only the percentage omits $120 of that amount. Compare the complete effective fee rate with settlement statements, and reverse unsupported vendor renewals through contractually permitted processes rather than stopping payments that keep the business operating.

Treat early-warning thresholds as company-specific circuit-breakers, not universal processor or lender rules. Track dispute count using each provider's prescribed denominator and period; separately track disputed dollars, refund dollars, fraud alerts, and unresolved fulfillment obligations. Set an internal alert below the provider's applicable program threshold and escalate any adverse provider notice immediately, since programs and account terms differ. For liquidity, produce a weekly thirteen-week cash forecast with payroll, taxes, debt service, inventory commitments, reserve releases, and customer receipts shown separately. Use an initial investigation trigger of less than six weeks of unavoidable cash outflow, then calibrate it to seasonal volatility and lender requirements. The canonical monthly operating-expense range is $6,000 to $25,000; six weeks approximates $22,500 to $105,000 using a four-week planning month, before separately modeled debt principal or exceptional commitments. Do not treat that range as a scenario-specific expense schedule. When thresholds trip, stop discretionary distributions, suspend unprofitable acquisition campaigns, investigate fulfillment defects, and negotiate terms before missing contractual payments. Keep required payroll, tax, and customer obligations visible during prioritization. The first hundred days should stabilize service and cash conversion before adding locations, hiring speculative teams, or automating an unreliable ledger into faster misinformation.

sections.heading: 4. Bound powered-land option losses and protect the acquisition's first hundred days
paragraphs: The seventh mapped play is ferc_grid_interconnection_queue_land_speculation: FERC / ISO Substation Interconnection Queue & Powered-Land Option Flipping, TRACK_1. Treat it as a bounded adjacent diligence exercise, not as ordinary acquired-business revenue or a substitute for operating earnings. Overlay public PJM, MISO, or CAISO interconnection queue records with county parcel boundaries, zoning, flood maps, recorded easements, and substation locations using QGIS. Queue entries primarily describe proposed projects and processes; they do not prove that an unrelated parcel has available load service, transferable interconnection rights, or construction-ready capacity. A nearby substation can have voltage, thermal, protection, or land-access constraints that make proximity economically useless. FERC Order No. 2023 reforms generator interconnection procedures, but the operative tariff, project status, utility service process, and applicable jurisdiction determine the actual requirements. For a prospective power-intensive tenant, obtain the utility's written load-service pathway rather than repurposing a generator queue position as a power commitment. Date-stamp every public source and record withdrawn projects instead of treating old screenshots as inventory. The fatal beginner trap is advertising secured power from a map overlay. If credible engineering, service timing, or land-use evidence fails, retain the research record and stop marketing claims that outrun the documented rights.

Bound the option economics before contacting landowners. Illustratively, three contingent options costing $10,000 each, $15,000 of shared engineering screening, and $5,000 of title and land-use work create $50,000 of initial exposure. Assume the documents impose no additional purchase, restoration, or extension obligation; verify that assumption rather than calling every option limited-risk. If one permitted assignment produces an $80,000 gross fee, the portfolio leaves $30,000 before overhead, taxes, financing, and other transaction expenses. That fee is the operator's consideration; neither the underlying parcel price nor a proposed tenant's electricity spending becomes operator revenue. With zero assignments, the modeled cash loss is $50,000, and delayed closing increases carrying costs wherever the contracts require them. Do not blend either result into the canonical acquisition scenarios. Confirm assignability, exclusivity, diligence access, extension charges, outside dates, recording rights, and seller termination remedies in each option. Use licensed transaction professionals where applicable brokerage rules require them. Negotiate engineering and utility contingencies before paying nonrefundable consideration. The explicit fallback is to let contingent options lapse or reposition land for independently viable uses without claiming secured power. A repositioning case must stand on its own demand, zoning, access, and economics, not on salvaging a sunk-cost narrative.

Return every adjacent opportunity to the acquisition's capital allocation discipline. The canonical startup capital range is $30,000 to $120,000 and time to first deal is six to eighteen months; neither describes cash that remains freely spendable after closing. Maintain separate balances for acquisition equity, transaction costs, operating liquidity, contractual reserves, and optional projects. A $50,000 speculative loss equals approximately 83% of Conservative annual owner profit and about 21% of Base profit before principal repayments. That asymmetry makes a modest-looking option program capable of destabilizing an otherwise sound purchase. During days one through thirty, validate opening balances, employee continuity, customer service, permit status, and collections. During days thirty-one through sixty, correct pricing leakage, renegotiate permissible vendor terms, and verify seller handoff obligations. During days sixty-one through one hundred, automate reconciled reporting and selected back-office workflows only after exception handling works manually. Keep the Scaled case's twelve-person staffing requirement visible; automation does not erase the canonical eight full-time employees and four contractors. Authorize optional investments only from genuinely available capital after satisfying documented operating and financing requirements. When evidence deteriorates, choose reversible actions: pause new commitments, preserve claim deadlines, reduce exposure, and renegotiate from current facts. A disciplined walkaway protects more capital than an elaborate recovery plan for a transaction whose cash economics never worked.

sections.heading: 1. Mine Demand Before Building the Seller List
paragraphs: Start with a buying thesis that identifies who pays, why they renew, and which operating constraint keeps competitors out. A useful first lane is recurring commercial service within a drivable territory: inspection, specialty repair, outsourced testing, or route-based services with documented repeat customers. Use Census County Business Patterns to size establishments, state licensing portals to identify qualified operators, and SAM.gov award records to locate recurring public buyers. An award is evidence of historical demand, not proof that its revenue transfers to a purchaser. Match each entity through its secretary-of-state record, operating website, business address, and license number before enrichment. Build 300 distinct accounts with source URLs, observation dates, ownership evidence, service territory, and a specific reason to investigate. Never infer retirement intent from a person's age or photo. A published succession statement, a broker listing, or a direct owner conversation is a usable signal. Keep the original observation separate from your interpretation in Airtable or HubSpot. This prevents a stale directory entry from becoming an invented seller motivation and makes weekly research reproducible when another analyst takes over the territory.

Map six acquisition-native plays and one adjacent tax-service play to evidence, not slogans. Renewal-Led Demand Mining tests whether repeat sales survive an ownership change: 40 customers paying $500 monthly represent $240,000 annual sales, before churn and delivery costs. License-and-Route Scarcity tests a capacity bottleneck: five additional weekly jobs at $180 yield $46,800 annual sales over 52 weeks, only if licensed labor and travel capacity exist. Retirement-Succession Outreach solves continuity rather than promising the highest bid; a 90-day handover at ten hours weekly requires about 130 owner hours, explicitly priced and scheduled. Referral-Partner Origination gives CPAs, attorneys, lenders, and trade suppliers a precise buyer brief, without demanding confidential client lists. Stalled-Listing Repricing targets documented gaps between asking price and supportable earnings. Working-Capital Recovery examines cash trapped in receivables and inventory without calling that release recurring profit. The seventh play, wotc_hourly_payroll_tax_credit_contingency_engine, can reveal service providers with employer relationships and weak documentation workflows. Treat it as a specialized diligence lane, not an automatic credit attached to every acquisition. Each play must have an observable trigger, a falsification test, and a fallback that still supports the business without speculative improvements.

Demand mining should uncover customer pain before you approach the seller with a valuation narrative. Review public procurement renewals, published inspection requirements, customer reviews, job advertisements, and branch openings. Record patterns such as repeated scheduling complaints or a new service territory, then test them through nonconfidential buyer interviews. Ask prospective customers what causes switching, how vendors qualify, and which work is deferred; do not pretend to represent the target. Ten interviews yielding six mentions of slow emergency response are a hypothesis, not six signed accounts. In the seller meeting, request service-level reports, renewal cohorts, cancellation reasons, and backlog aging to corroborate the pattern. Give each signal a freshness date and a confidence label supported by its source. A license renewal approaching expiration can indicate administrative workload, but it does not establish willingness to sell. Route density likewise requires actual stop locations and dispatch records, shared under appropriate confidentiality terms. If those records contradict the public story, revise the thesis immediately. The best sourcing advantage is knowing which demand is transferable, collectible, and profitable before spending heavily on exclusivity, lenders, and outside diligence specialists.

sections.heading: 2. Turn Public Signals into Permission-Based Seller Conversations
paragraphs: Run a measured 30-day account cadence rather than a blast campaign. On day one, send a short business email identifying the buyer, the acquisition thesis, and the specific operating feature that attracted attention. Ask whether an ownership-continuity discussion would be useful; do not imply that you already have a valuation or committed lender. On day four, make a manual business call during local business hours and leave one factual message when appropriate. On day nine, mail a concise buyer letter to the published business address. On day sixteen, follow up through email or an existing professional introduction with one relevant question about transition timing. On day thirty, close the loop and stop unless the owner requests further contact. Apply 15 U.S.C. § 7704 where commercial-email rules govern: accurate headers, nondeceptive subjects, required identification, a valid postal address, and a functioning opt-out. Honor covered opt-outs within ten business days and suppress them sooner operationally. Evaluate 47 U.S.C. § 227 and applicable state restrictions before calls or texts; avoid automated dialing, prerecorded messages, and unsolicited texting as default sourcing methods.

Use funnel arithmetic as a planning hypothesis, not an industry promise. From 300 researched businesses, suppose 240 have verified, lawfully usable contact routes. If 48 owners engage meaningfully, the contact-to-conversation rate is 20%; if 24 accept a discovery meeting, the conversation-to-meeting rate is 50%. Twelve signed confidentiality agreements would represent 50% of those meetings. Six complete initial data packs would represent 50% of signed agreements; three indications of interest would represent 50% of complete packs. One accepted letter of intent from three indications is approximately 33%, and one completed acquisition from that letter requires successful diligence, funding, and closing conditions. The end-to-end illustration is one closing from 300 researched accounts, or approximately 0.33%, not a dependable forecast. Define the first three to ten sourcing wins as diligence-ready opportunities: a willing seller, agreed transaction perimeter, basic records, and a credible funding path. Track completed purchases separately. A first-time operator should not reinterpret ten sourcing wins as ten simultaneous acquisitions; each closing creates integration work and capital exposure. Review conversion by source cohort monthly instead of blending referrals with cold outbound.

Create inbound credibility with a one-page buyer site describing target sectors, geography, operating involvement, capital range, and a secure contact route. Publish a sample acquisition process and explain which records are requested at each stage; do not publish fabricated portfolio logos or lender commitments. A downloadable seller-preparation checklist can attract serious owners without collecting tax returns through an open web form. Use role-based access and an invitation-only document room after confidentiality terms are signed. Allocate an illustrative $3,000 monthly sourcing budget across research, postage, CRM, and travel; over six months, $18,000 divided by six diligence-ready opportunities equals $3,000 per opportunity. At one closing, the same spend equals $18,000 acquisition sourcing cost before legal, accounting, and lender expenses. If the cohort produces no closing, report the spend and zero closings rather than manufacturing a cost per acquisition. Review partner referrals, direct mail, and inbound separately. Twelve partner meetings producing three introductions and one complete data pack reveal where to improve the brief. Do not pay transaction-based referral compensation until counsel has evaluated the transaction, intermediary activities, and applicable federal and state requirements.

sections.heading: 3. Qualify Earnings, Liabilities, and the Tax-Service Edge Case
paragraphs: Score opportunities before negotiating exclusivity. Allocate 25 points to earnings evidence, 20 to customer durability, 15 to management transferability, 15 to working-capital quality, 15 to funding feasibility, and ten to transaction readiness. Within each category, award zero for an unsupported assertion, half credit for partial documents, and full credit only for corroborated evidence. A score of 75 can justify deeper work, but it cannot override a disqualifier such as an essential nontransferable license or an unexplained cash discrepancy. Obtain 24–36 months of monthly statements, tax returns through authorized channels, bank records, payroll registers, aged receivables, and customer concentration. Reconcile recognized sales to collections with an explicit bridge for receivables, deposits, refunds, and timing. An add-back is acceptable only when the expense genuinely disappears without replacement cost or revenue damage. If claimed earnings are $250,000 and a necessary replacement manager costs $80,000 fully loaded, the preliminary adjusted figure is $170,000 before other corrections. Do not apply an acquisition multiple to the larger number simply because a listing labels owner labor optional. Commission independent QoE work where transaction size and complexity justify its cost.

Investigate liabilities through entity, asset, and contract trails, not solely through a seller questionnaire. Search the relevant state UCC filing office, inspect tax liens and litigation records where available, and request payoff statements for secured debt. Search results establish a research trail rather than proving that every liability has been located. Counsel should evaluate continuing security interests under the applicable state enactment of UCC § 9-315 and obtain effective releases where required. An asset purchase does not automatically eliminate employment, tax, environmental, or other successor exposure. Map contract assignment provisions, customer termination rights, license changes, and required third-party permissions. For qualifying federal contract transfers, assess FAR 42.1204 rather than assuming a SAM.gov award moves with the equipment. Investigate wage practices against applicable federal and state rules, including 29 U.S.C. §§ 206 and 207 where covered. Translate each unresolved issue into a specific response: price adjustment, retained liability, escrow, indemnity, preclosing cure, or withdrawal. A seller representation is not a substitute for an operational remedy. Ask whether losing the largest customer or key license holder would still leave enough cash for wages, suppliers, interest, and scheduled principal.

The wotc_hourly_payroll_tax_credit_contingency_engine requires separate workflows for Section 51 hiring credits and Section 41 research credits. Before modeling WOTC, verify the operative Section 51(c)(4) hire-date limitation and any enacted extension; do not assume post-2025 hires qualify. For eligible hires, employer-authorized prescreening, timely Form 8850 submission to the designated state agency, certification, hours, and qualified wages support the claim. The general submission deadline is 28 days after work begins, subject to applicable rules and relief. Ten certified employees with $6,000 eligible wages each and the standard 40% rate would generate $24,000 credits, assuming the applicable 400-hour threshold and all other requirements. A hypothetical 15% outcome-linked fee would be $3,600 service revenue only where that arrangement is permitted; the employer's $24,000 credit is not operator revenue. Evaluate professional restrictions, including 31 CFR 10.27 where applicable. Section 41 separately requires qualified research activities and substantiated expenses; routine software use does not establish eligibility. Reconcile wage use across incentives and apply Section 280C adjustments where required. Exclude unsupported claims and use fixed-fee payroll and research-documentation services under independent tax review when outcome-linked economics cannot be supported.

callout.title: Four Checks Before Paying for Exclusivity and Full Diligence
callout.body: A high sourcing score cannot compensate for missing authority, unsupported earnings, or an unworkable transfer.
items: Verify the seller's authority and the exact asset or equity perimeter; identify excluded assets, related-party leases, and essential operating permissions.
Tie preliminary earnings to bank, payroll, and tax evidence; price replacement management and document every accepted add-back.
Obtain lender feedback on the proposed structure, equity contribution, seller-note treatment, and postclosing liquidity before presenting funding as credible.
For tax-service targets, independently test program authorization dates, claim documentation, wage coordination, and fee restrictions before assigning value to the backlog.

sections.heading: 4. Convert Qualified Opportunities into Fundable Offers and a Controlled First Closing
paragraphs: Sequence the first 4–10 months around evidence milestones. Use months one through three to refine the thesis, establish capital capacity, build the account universe, and test outreach messages. Use months four through six to deepen partner introductions, complete seller discovery, and assemble three to ten credible opportunities as the pipeline permits. The remaining period covers indications of interest, exclusivity, QoE, lender underwriting, definitive agreements, and a controlled first closing. These are planning windows, not deadlines that justify lowering standards. An indication should state the earnings basis, valuation method, working-capital assumption, proposed consideration, and remaining evidence requirements. A letter of intent should distinguish binding provisions from the proposed transaction terms and define access, exclusivity duration, and expense responsibility with counsel. Offer sellers certainty through a visible diligence calendar rather than an inflated headline price followed by predictable retrading. For example, reducing claimed earnings from $200,000 to $170,000 changes an illustrative three-times value from $600,000 to $510,000, a $90,000 difference. Explain the documented replacement cost causing that change. If price expectations remain incompatible, preserve the relationship and revisit after new evidence rather than manufacturing an earnout neither party can administer.

Keep canonical operating cases distinct from acquisition consideration and illustrative sourcing math. Conservative sales are $750,000 at 8%, producing $60,000 annual owner net profit with seven full-time employees and three contractors. Base sales are $1,875,000 at 13.0%, producing $243,750 with the same team. Scaled sales are $3,000,000 at 18%, producing $540,000 with eight full-time employees and four contractors, twelve people total. These margins are after interest and before principal repayments. Purchase proceeds paid to the seller, lender advances, and released working capital are not acquired-business sales. As a separate cash bridge, $243,750 Base profit less $90,000 scheduled annual principal leaves $153,750 before capital spending, working-capital changes, and any other cash adjustments. Do not subtract interest a second time. Startup capital of $30,000–$120,000 and monthly operating outlays of $6,000–$25,000 are planning ranges, not a substitute for a complete target cost structure. Reconcile all payroll, delivery costs, overhead, and interest to the canonical margins rather than forcing annual costs into that monthly range. Do not add the tax-service example's hypothetical fees to these cases; they are diligence illustrations, not extra scorecard revenue.

Structure funding around verified repayment capacity and the lender's current requirements. For an SBA-backed transaction, confirm eligibility, change-of-ownership rules, equity injection, seller-note treatment, collateral, and guaranties against current SBA requirements and the lender's written interpretation. 13 CFR 120.110 identifies ineligible business categories, while 13 CFR 120.150 addresses credit criteria; neither replaces the applicable operating procedures or transaction-specific underwriting. Do not assume a seller note counts as equity or permits immediate payments. Negotiate its standby, subordination, maturity, and payment provisions explicitly. For an applicable asset acquisition, coordinate purchase-price allocation under 26 U.S.C. § 1060 and required Form 8594 reporting. Prepare the first 100 days before signing: payroll continuity, bank access, customer introductions, vendor terms, license coverage, reporting, and a weekly cash forecast. Automate bank-feed reconciliation, invoice routing, and management reporting only after control owners and exception handling are assigned. Keep the seller available for scheduled relationship transfers and document completion. Stop adding acquisitions when integration capacity is exhausted, even if sourcing remains productive. A signed letter records intent; a completed purchase with intact customers, functioning payroll, and supported liquidity is the actual operating win.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #13, Business Acquisition, ranks #17 with a 86/100 Money-to-Manpower Score: ownership produces cash only when diligence survives operating reality. This chapter connects seven mapped plays: acquisition sourcing, Quality of Earnings, SBA and seller-note structuring, controlled closing, customer-retention turnaround, reporting automation, and commercial solar partnership-flip investing. sections.heading: 1. Move one acquisition through seven evidence-backed operating plays
paragraphs: Start acquisition sourcing with a written buy box, not a broker spreadsheet sorted by advertised earnings. Assign every target a permanent internal identifier and record industry, operating geography, seller authority, customer concentration, required licenses, and the source of each earnings claim. Keep target leads separate from the acquired company's customer orders: neither an introduction nor a signed letter of intent creates operator revenue. The seven mapped plays in this chapter are acquisition sourcing, Quality of Earnings, SBA and seller-note structuring, controlled closing, customer-retention turnaround, reporting automation, and commercial solar partnership-flip investing. The first six are acquisition workflow labels; the seventh carries the supplied specialist play identifier. Give each play an accountable owner, an evidence packet, and a rejection condition before spending more money. For example, twelve reviewed targets producing four credible diligence candidates means eight documented scrubs, not eight unexplained CRM deletions. Retain the rejected records so the next broker email cannot resurrect a known title defect under a different business name. Budget the actual six-to-eighteen-month search horizon and $30,000–$120,000 startup capital range. The ninety-day walkthrough begins after an anchor acquisition closes; it does not compress that search into three months.

Quality of Earnings converts the seller's story into a reproducible earnings bridge. Request twenty-four months of bank statements, general-ledger exports, payroll registers, sales-tax filings, receivables aging, merchant settlements, and customer-level invoices. Tie monthly invoice totals to recognized sales, then explain the timing difference between sales and deposits. A seller claiming $300,000 of adjusted earnings with $45,000 of personal expenses and $35,000 of allegedly temporary wages has not established $380,000 of maintainable earnings. Accept the personal-expense adjustment only with underlying receipts and replacement-cost analysis; retain the wages if the work continues after transfer. If both adjustments fail, underwrite $300,000, then deduct any missing market-rate management cost. Use QuickBooks Online or Xero exports as source inputs, not independent proof of cash. Match bank-originated statements and inspect subsequent receipts on overdue invoices. Separate refundable customer deposits, unearned subscriptions, and sales tax collected from earned revenue. Trace concentrated customers through signed contracts and actual renewal behavior, because a $150,000 annual account represents eight percent of Base sales. Losing that account cannot be repaired by renaming acquisition debt as working capital. Escalate unexplained differences to the diligence lead before revising the purchase price.

SBA and seller-note structuring starts with a sources-and-uses schedule that balances to the dollar. In an illustrative $700,000 funding package, $450,000 of senior debt, $100,000 of seller debt, and $150,000 of buyer equity fund $600,000 of purchase consideration, $40,000 of transaction costs, and $60,000 of opening working capital. This example illustrates structure, not the cohort's debt amortization or an assertion of lender acceptance. Obtain the lender's written treatment of seller-note standby, equity injection, collateral, distributions, and scheduled principal. Apply 13 CFR 120.110 to borrower eligibility and 13 CFR 120.160 to applicable loan conditions; never infer eligibility from a broker's use of the term SBA. Controlled closing then resolves asset ownership, lien releases, assigned contracts, employment obligations, licenses, and the final working-capital adjustment. UCC § 9-315 explains why a security interest may continue in transferred collateral unless an applicable exception or authorization resolves it. For covered asset acquisitions, coordinate the buyer's and seller's allocation under 26 U.S.C. § 1060. Keep transfer taxes, escrow holdbacks, and purchase consideration out of operating sales. A signed closing binder establishes contractual completion; bank evidence and the ledger establish where the money actually went.

callout.title: Four diligence habits that survive seller handover
callout.body: Build evidence that remains useful after the seller stops answering daily questions.
items: Request a bank-originated statement for the first full month after the reporting cutoff; subsequent collections often expose receivable inflation faster than another earnings presentation.
Create a replacement-cost schedule for every seller duty, including quoting, dispatch, purchasing, and collections; one departing owner can conceal several distinct jobs.
Negotiate a named working-capital peg and account-by-account inclusions before exclusivity expires; exclude stale inventory and disputed receivables through explicit definitions.
Keep the seller's existing customer-facing phone numbers and dispatch routines stable during the first payroll cycle; change reporting controls before changing familiar service touchpoints.

sections.heading: 2. Implement six transactional modules from target intake to bank reconciliation
paragraphs: The production boundary is deliberately narrow: one authorized acquisition entity, one USD ledger, a local SQLite database, and no payment initiation. Copy the six modules below into one Python file in order and execute it with Python 3.9 or later. They define callable functions rather than importing customer files or contacting banks automatically. Store the database on a local filesystem with reliable SQLite locking, not a shared network drive. Every mutation opens its own connection and obtains BEGIN IMMEDIATE before reading mutable state. Consequently, concurrent writers serialize before making decisions; uniqueness constraints remain the final defense against duplicate targets, events, and bank matches. A thirty-second lock timeout surfaces an error instead of quietly dropping a write. Retry the same operation identifier and identical payload after a timeout. The operation journal returns the previous result for an identical retry and rejects changed content under an existing identifier. This guarantee covers these functions on this database, not arbitrary administrator SQL, shared-drive locking failures, or a bank's independent systems. There is no read-then-write window outside the transaction and no external transfer whose success could be mistaken for a local commit.

Treat documents as immutable evidence references, not as attachments that silently change beneath a completed review. The evidence function accepts a SHA-256 digest and a reviewer-controlled reference; store the corresponding encrypted document in the authorized project repository with role-based access. A digest proves content identity, not document truth. The controller must verify bank origin, signer authority, and the actual legal requirement before accepting each evidence kind. The state machine advances only from intake to verified, then escrow_ready, then closed. It does not initiate escrow, authorize a wire, or replace the closing agent. The final state records reviewed settlement evidence; reconciliation can still expose an accounting exception afterward. Corrections should create a new documented transaction or a separately reviewed migration, never overwrite an old evidence hash. The intake score is a transparent local screening heuristic using margin and concentration; it is unrelated to the volume's 86/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Keep those labels separate in dashboards. The stored version increments during state changes, while the write transaction prevents another worker from changing the predecessor state mid-decision. Do not expose these write functions directly as unauthenticated web endpoints.

The ledger uses signed integer cents: debits are positive, credits negative, and every journal must sum to zero. A credit sale posts receivables against sales; collection posts cash against receivables; interest is an expense; principal reduces debt. Purchase consideration belongs in acquisition accounting, not customer revenue. The reference permits at most one cash line per journal so a statement transaction has exactly one candidate cash amount. Split merchant batches through a clearing-account design before extending this minimal model; do not force a many-to-many settlement into the one-to-one matching rule. Bank statements retain stable account and transaction identifiers, and a match is accepted only when signed amounts agree. Reconciliation shows both unmatched ledger cash and unmatched bank transactions, rather than hiding one side with an inner join. The QA routine reads a consistent snapshot, checks journal balance and foreign keys, and optionally requires every cash item to reconcile. Back up through SQLite's backup interface and test restoration before relying on a quarter-end close. These are reference controls requiring local execution and review, not a claim that the supplied code has been run against the operator's private books or banking feeds.

headers: Module and execution boundary
Copy-pasteable Python and SQL implementation
Concurrency and integrity invariant
Operator acceptance evidence
rows: Module 1: initialize schema and transactional idempotency infrastructure

import hashlib
import json
import os
import sqlite3

DB = os.environ.get("FYMC_LEDGER_DB", "acquisition.sqlite3")

def connect():
    db = sqlite3.connect(DB, timeout=30, isolation_level=None)
    db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
    db.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000")
    db.execute("PRAGMA synchronous=FULL")
    return db

def digest(value):
    raw = json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
    return hashlib.sha256(raw.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

db = connect()
try:
    db.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
    db.executescript('''
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS operations (
    op_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    payload_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    result_json TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS deals (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    target_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    payload_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    annual_sales_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(annual_sales_cents > 0),
    normalized_profit_cents INTEGER NOT NULL,
    largest_customer_bps INTEGER NOT NULL
        CHECK(largest_customer_bps BETWEEN 0 AND 10000),
    screen_score INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(screen_score BETWEEN 0 AND 100),
    state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'intake'
        CHECK(state IN ('intake','verified','escrow_ready','closed')),
    version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS evidence (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    deal_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES deals(id),
    kind TEXT NOT NULL,
    reference TEXT NOT NULL,
    sha256 TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(length(sha256) = 64),
    UNIQUE(deal_id, kind)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS journals (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    source TEXT NOT NULL,
    event_key TEXT NOT NULL,
    effective_date TEXT NOT NULL,
    memo TEXT NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE(source, event_key)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS lines (
    journal_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES journals(id),
    line_number INTEGER NOT NULL,
    account TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(account IN
        ('1000','1100','1500','2000','2500','3000','4000','5000','6100','7100')),
    cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(typeof(cents) = 'integer' AND cents != 0),
    UNIQUE(journal_id, line_number)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS statements (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    bank_account TEXT NOT NULL,
    bank_event TEXT NOT NULL,
    effective_date TEXT NOT NULL,
    cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(typeof(cents) = 'integer' AND cents != 0),
    UNIQUE(bank_account, bank_event)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS matches (
    journal_id INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES journals(id),
    statement_id INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES statements(id)
);
''')
finally:
    db.close()

def transact(op_id, payload, work):
    payload_hash = digest(payload)
    db = connect()
    try:
        db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        prior = db.execute(
            "SELECT payload_hash, result_json FROM operations WHERE op_id=?",
            (op_id,),
        ).fetchone()
        if prior:
            if prior[0] != payload_hash:
                raise ValueError("Operation identifier reused with changed content")
            result = json.loads(prior[1])
            db.commit()
            return result
        result = work(db)
        db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO operations VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
            (op_id, payload_hash, json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True)),
        )
        db.commit()
        return result
    except Exception:
        if db.in_transaction:
            db.rollback()
        raise
    finally:
        db.close()
Immediate transactions serialize writers before any mutable decision reads
Two identical concurrent requests produce one stored operation result
Module 2: score intake without duplicating the target identity
Permanent target uniqueness prevents duplicate broker submissions becoming deals
Changed metrics under the same identity raise a review exception
Module 3: attach verified evidence and serialize closing-state transitions
Evidence inspection and predecessor checks share the same write transaction
Two competing advances cannot skip or overwrite a closing state
Module 4: post balanced integer-cent journals with stable event keys
Journal header, all lines, and retry result commit atomically
Repeated source events cannot add revenue or cash a second time
Module 5: import bank records and expose both reconciliation sides
Unique matches prevent two workers consuming the same bank transaction
Unmatched statement records remain visible even without ledger counterparts
Module 6: inspect a consistent close snapshot and assert invariants

def qa(require_reconciled=True):
    db = connect()
    try:
        db.execute("BEGIN")
        integrity = db.execute("PRAGMA integrity_check").fetchall()
        foreign_keys = db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_key_check").fetchall()
        bad_journals = db.execute(
            "SELECT j.id FROM journals j LEFT JOIN lines l ON l.journal_id=j.id "
            "GROUP BY j.id HAVING COUNT(l.line_number)<2 "
            "OR COALESCE(SUM(l.cents),0)!=0 "
            "OR SUM(CASE WHEN l.account='1000' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)>1"
        ).fetchall()
        bad_matches = db.execute(
            "SELECT m.journal_id FROM matches m "
            "JOIN statements s ON s.id=m.statement_id "
            "LEFT JOIN lines l ON l.journal_id=m.journal_id AND l.account='1000' "
            "GROUP BY m.journal_id,s.cents "
            "HAVING COUNT(l.line_number)!=1 OR COALESCE(SUM(l.cents),0)!=s.cents"
        ).fetchall()
        exceptions = db.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM cash_reconciliation WHERE status!='matched'"
        ).fetchall()
        if integrity != [("ok",)] or foreign_keys or bad_journals or bad_matches:
            raise AssertionError("Ledger integrity or journal invariant failed")
        if require_reconciled and exceptions:
            raise AssertionError("Unresolved bank reconciliation items: "
                                 + str(len(exceptions)))
        cash_cents = db.execute(
            "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cents),0) FROM lines WHERE account='1000'"
        ).fetchone()[0]
        db.commit()
        return {"cash_cents": cash_cents, "reconciliation_exceptions": exceptions}
    except Exception:
        if db.in_transaction:
            db.rollback()
        raise
    finally:
        db.close()
Snapshot reads cannot mix balances from different concurrent commits
Close requires balanced journals and an explicitly resolved exception queue

sections.heading: 3. Stabilize payroll, customers, debt service, and specialist investments
paragraphs: Customer-retention turnaround begins with service continuity, not a new logo or an immediate systems migration. On the first operating day, confirm payroll funding, insurance effectiveness, supplier credit, dispatch coverage, customer contacts, and access to invoicing. Map the Base team of seven full-time employees to a general manager, an operations lead, four delivery staff, and an administrative coordinator; three contractors provide bookkeeping, specialist technical support, and overflow delivery. These are illustrative roles within the canonical headcount, not permission to classify employees as contractors contrary to the governing facts. Review wage, overtime, benefit, and classification obligations before changing schedules. At this illustrative size, federal WARN coverage is not established merely by the acquisition; test the actual employer and transaction facts under 29 U.S.C. § 2101 and examine applicable state requirements separately. Contact the twenty largest accounts with the seller where permitted, confirm open orders, and log any request to renegotiate. If two $10,000 monthly accounts pause purchases, the $20,000 sales gap is nearly thirteen percent of Base monthly sales. Assign recovery ownership immediately, but preserve contribution by avoiding an indiscriminate ten-percent discount across the whole book.

Reporting automation should shorten the time between a mistake and its discovery. Export invoices, receipts, payroll summaries, and payables on a fixed daily schedule; preserve source event identifiers rather than generating new identifiers on every import. Use Microsoft Power Automate for controlled file routing or a scheduled Python job for validated imports, while leaving posting authority with the controller. Each morning, inspect yesterday's cash exceptions, overdue collections, dispatch failures, and payroll funding. Each Friday, refresh a thirteen-week cash forecast that separates interest, scheduled principal, replacement equipment, taxes, and owner distributions. The Base scorecard recognizes $1,875,000 of annual sales and $243,750 of owner profit after interest but before principal. That definition does not establish distributable cash. In the worked quarter, $15,000 of principal and $1,562.50 of additional receivables reduce $60,937.50 of profit to $44,375 of cash generation. Do not claim an automated reporting workflow raises the canonical margin above thirteen percent without a separately supported scenario. If a connector changes its export format, quarantine the batch, preserve the raw file, and reconcile the previous accepted batch before attempting a corrected import. Reversals must remain visible as new journals.

The specialist mapped play solar_tax_equity_depreciation_strip_syndication concerns Commercial Solar Tax-Equity Flip & Bonus-Depreciation Strip Syndication, TRACK_1. Treat it as a separately underwritten investment structure, not an automatic extension of buying an operating company. Commercial solar partnership-flip investments allocate supported tax benefits and cash flows to genuine equity owners; depreciation cannot be sold as a standalone credit. Consider a separate project with $1,000,000 of genuine equity and an investor contributing $100,000. If independently reviewed economics support a ten-percent allocation of $200,000 of allowable depreciation for the relevant period, the allocated deduction is $20,000, not $20,000 of cash revenue. A ten-percent share of $30,000 of distributable project cash would produce $3,000 before investor-specific effects, assuming that allocation matches the documented waterfall. Neither percentage is established merely by the capital contribution. Review 26 U.S.C. § 704 allocation requirements, § 168 depreciation rules, § 7701(o) economic substance where relevant, and securities registration or exemption requirements under 15 U.S.C. § 77e. Do not add project capital, tax deductions, or investor distributions to the acquisition scorecard's operating sales. If structure or authority is deficient, suspend solicitation and closing, use appropriately licensed intermediaries, and restructure only as independently reviewed genuine equity ownership.

sections.heading: 4. Walk three operating months from separate lead cohorts to reconciled cash
paragraphs: The Worked 90-Day Cohort Walk begins with one acquired operating company already closed on day zero, $100,000 of available operating cash, and $15,625 of collectible opening receivables. Purchase consideration, transaction costs, and financing proceeds belong to the separately reconciled closing schedule and do not appear as quarter revenue. The $100,000 opening reserve is a cohort assumption, not a claim that it equals all startup capital. Month 1, Month 2, and Month 3 also originate twelve, ten, and eight acquisition leads respectively. Eight, seven, and six leads are scrubbed for concentration, unsupported earnings, or transfer defects; four, three, and two remain active from their respective cohorts. No additional acquisition closes during this walkthrough, so the nine surviving leads create neither sales nor a speculative valuation gain. Routine screening costs are included in overhead; no separate add-on diligence invoice is assumed. For the anchor business, ninety percent of each month's sales is collected that month and ten percent the next month. All opening receivables collect in Month 1. There are no modeled customer write-offs, refunds, inventory changes, or unpaid operating bills; actual exceptions require an explicit revised cash bridge.

Monthly sales are $140,625, $156,250, and $171,875, totaling $468,750. Direct delivery costs equal sixty-five percent of sales: $91,406.25, $101,562.50, and $111,718.75. Operating overhead is $27,437.50, $30,875, and $34,312.50, while interest is $3,500 each month. Overhead falls inside the supplied $6,000–$25,000 monthly operating expense planning range under this model's classification; total expenses also include direct delivery and interest. Each month therefore retains thirteen percent owner profit: $18,281.25, $20,312.50, and $22,343.75. The quarter's $60,937.50 multiplies by four to the canonical $243,750 Base annual profit, and quarterly sales multiply by four to $1,875,000. Month 2 equals the Base monthly run rate exactly. Month 3 represents a seasonal increase within the same quarter, not a new annual forecast or the Scaled case. Costs are paid in the month incurred, and the model includes no additional tax, capital expenditure, or owner-distribution cash line. Those exclusions are modeling boundaries rather than assertions that an actual buyer never incurs them. Keep scheduled principal below profit so the scorecard's after-interest, before-principal basis remains unchanged throughout the walkthrough.

Collection timing produces cash receipts of $142,187.50 in Month 1, $154,687.50 in Month 2, and $170,312.50 in Month 3. Month 1 includes $126,562.50 from current sales plus the $15,625 opening receivables; Month 2 includes $140,625 plus $14,062.50; Month 3 includes $154,687.50 plus $15,625. Total receipts are therefore $467,187.50, exactly $1,562.50 below recognized sales. Ending receivables are $17,187.50, which explains that difference against the $15,625 opening balance. After $407,812.50 of direct costs, overhead, and interest, operating cash generation is $59,375. Subtract three illustrative $5,000 principal payments to obtain $44,375 of cash generation after principal. Ending cash is $144,375, with no owner distribution assumed. The independent bridge reaches the same answer: $60,937.50 owner profit minus $1,562.50 receivables growth minus $15,000 principal equals $44,375. Record principal against debt, not interest expense, and retain the lender's actual amortization schedule because the illustrative payment is not derived from the earlier funding example. At day ninety, export the reconciliation exceptions, bank balances, receivables aging, and debt rollforward together. A strong quarter is evidenced by this closed cash bridge, not by the number of leads still sitting in the acquisition pipeline.

sections.heading: 1. Build a jurisdiction-aware directory before building a target list
paragraphs: Organize the acquisition desk around seven explicitly mapped plays: P1 target origination, P2 entity verification, P3 liability discovery, P4 revenue validation, P5 QoE normalization, P6 financing structure, and P7 the 100-day turnaround. These are this chapter's operating labels, not seven additional businesses or revenue streams. Assign every collected field to a play and a decision: a former legal name improves lien searches; a permit expiration changes the transition calendar; bank settlements challenge recorded sales. For the seven-full-time, three-contractor model, a practical allocation is an owner-operator, an operating manager, an administrative controller, and four delivery employees, supported by contracted transaction counsel, a QoE accountant, and an integration specialist. These are capacity assignments within the four-person envelope, not hires layered onto the scorecard. The delivery employees protect customer service while the owner and controller maintain the evidence queue. During the search period, the buyer and retained specialists cover those functions before the acquired operating team transfers. Keep only enough active diligence files to inspect each exception weekly; software cannot make ten people simultaneously operate the business, rebuild its books, and close several transactions.

Start each target with a jurisdiction map containing formation state, operating locations, property counties, historical names, and license issuers. Secretary of State records establish filed identity and status, not the actual ownership of every entity. An organizer or registered agent is not automatically an owner. Apply enacted state versions of UCC sections 9-301, 9-307, 9-503, and 9-507 when choosing filing offices and debtor-name searches; fixture filings and certain collateral require additional treatment. A web search result is a lead, while a dated official search report supports a transaction workpaper. Search federal litigation through PACER and state litigation through the relevant judiciary because neither substitutes for the other. County land records can expose mortgages, recorded liens, and property transfers, but tax-lien filing locations vary with applicable rules and property type. Treat every negative result as scoped evidence: record the name, office, date range, and indexing limitations. A clean screen never establishes that all liabilities are absent. Have counsel define closing search coverage, payoff evidence, and termination deliverables rather than letting an entity matching script decide whether a lien has disappeared.

Use the directory below as an acquisition-specific retrieval plan, not a claim that every portal offers bulk access. Cost descriptions distinguish public viewing, transaction charges, and negotiated commercial products; verify current prices before procurement. Refresh descriptions describe source behavior rather than promised delivery times. Capture both source publication time and retrieval time so a fresh download does not disguise old underlying records. For an API, read the documented quota, respect Retry-After when provided, and use bounded exponential backoff with jitter. For a human-only portal, perform a documented manual search or purchase its authorized export instead of bypassing access controls. Preserve search receipts and source files because public interfaces change during a six-to-eighteen-month deal cycle. Do not infer loan balances from SBA origination datasets, transferable permits from active license displays, or customer retention from federal award totals. Each source earns its place only when it changes outreach, price, structure, or a post-close operating action. The controller owns provenance; counsel interprets legal findings; the owner decides whether the evidence justifies spending the next diligence dollar or extending exclusivity.

sections.heading: 2. Run an evidence-first enrichment waterfall with explicit stop rules
paragraphs: Run enrichment in a fixed order: official entity identity, company-owned website, licensed business directory, commercial contact discovery, and human verification. OpenCorporates can help connect legal names and jurisdictions, but confirm decisive facts against the filing office and license API access under its current terms. Apollo can suggest business contacts; Hunter can test domain-based email hypotheses; neither establishes ownership, authority to sell, or permission to retrieve private records. Store each provider's claim separately rather than overwriting an official fact with a higher-confidence marketing score. A target record needs a stable internal identifier, legal-name history, formation identifier, website domain, operating address, source timestamp, and match rationale. Require at least two independent matching attributes before merging records, and send shared addresses, common names, and franchise locations to human review. Stop buying credits when the legal entity is unresolved or the business falls outside the owner's acquisition criteria. A cheap contact attached to the wrong debtor can create expensive diligence work, mistaken outreach, and an incorrect concentration analysis later. Preserve rejected matches so the next provider cannot silently recreate the same mistake.

Set a deliberately small enrichment allowance inside the existing operating budget rather than describing subscriptions as incremental profit. As an illustrative purchasing rule, authorize $300 monthly for screening 100 named targets: $3 per screened target before labor and specialist work. If only 20 targets meet the mandate, that becomes $15 per qualified target, not $3. Three seller conversations would imply $100 of subscription expense per conversation, without proving that enrichment caused any conversation. Use these denominators to cancel tools that produce decorative coverage. Do not extrapolate this screening budget into deal economics or replace the canonical $6,000–$25,000 monthly operating-expense range with it. The owner approves target criteria, the controller manages provider credits, and the integration contractor maintains connectors within a capped assignment. Counsel reviews permitted use where a product includes personal information. Keep commercial outreach accurate and apply the concrete requirements of 15 U.S.C. 7704 when sending commercial email, including truthful headers, required sender details, and functioning opt-out handling. A verified address measures deliverability; it does not erase messaging obligations or justify repeated contact after suppression.

Implement the first pipeline with Python's csv, json, sqlite3, hashlib, and urllib modules before buying an orchestration platform. Store immutable source artifacts separately from normalized SQLite tables, then attach artifact hashes, retrieval times, request parameters, and transformation versions to each derived finding. Keep API credentials outside exports and redact tokens from request logs. Use least-privilege database roles where the deployed database supports them; protect local SQLite files through operating-system permissions and encrypted storage. Idempotent imports should key records by source and native identifier, with versioned snapshots for changing fields. Test entity collisions, empty pages, repeated cursors, deleted transactions, changed accounting periods, and malformed currency strings. Quarantine incomplete responses rather than converting missing amounts to zero. Maintain a queue with severity, owner, due date, evidence link, and decision impact. Only the owner and controller need routine access to the acquisition dashboard; delivery employees receive the operational tasks relevant to their work. This keeps P1 through P7 connected without exposing payroll, customer contracts, or seller bank details across the entire four-person pod. Review access again when a bidder withdraws or a contractor finishes.

callout.title: Four ways experienced buyers prevent expensive false certainty
callout.body: Spend enrichment credits on resolved entities and reserve specialist time for findings capable of changing the transaction.
items: Build the historical debtor-name list before ordering UCC searches; include documented mergers and name changes so counsel can determine the correct search coverage.
Compare operating addresses across permits, payroll locations, and customer invoices; a mailing address alone can conceal an unreviewed operating site.
Use accounting document numbers and bank settlement references as reconciliation anchors; matching only dates and amounts breaks when deposits are batched.
Retain rejected entity matches with reasons; otherwise a refreshed commercial dataset can reintroduce a previously disproved owner or subsidiary relationship.

sections.heading: 3. Turn permissioned records into a reproducible QoE and financing bridge
paragraphs: Move from public research to seller-authorized access only after defining the entity, period, purpose, and recipients of each dataset. Request monthly trial balances, general ledgers, bank statements, accounts-receivable aging, payroll registers, tax returns, and customer-level sales for a consistent diligence period. QuickBooks OAuth authorization must come from an authorized account administrator, and permissions must be limited to what the platform actually supports; do not advertise a read-only restriction that the granted scope does not enforce. Where appropriate, use controlled accountant exports instead. Plaid access similarly requires authorized connection of the relevant accounts, supported institutions, and an agreed retention policy. Public registries do not expose confidential federal tax returns: 26 U.S.C. 6103 governs disclosure, and seller-provided returns or properly authorized transcript procedures serve a different evidentiary role. Do not substitute personal consumer reports for ordinary business diligence. If a proposed report is covered by the Fair Credit Reporting Act, establish an actual permissible purpose under 15 U.S.C. 1681b and applicable procedural duties before ordering it. A signed acquisition interest letter alone does not create unrestricted access to personal records.

Build the revenue bridge from invoices to ledger postings, settlement batches, bank deposits, and reported tax figures, preserving timing differences explicitly. Separate sales taxes collected, customer deposits, loan proceeds, owner contributions, refunds, chargebacks, and transfers between accounts. A deposit is not automatically revenue; an invoice is not automatically cash. For marketplace or payment businesses, distinguish merchant throughput from the target's recognized fees. For this candidate, the scorecard revenue basis is acquired-business sales, not acquisition purchase price, borrowed principal, or a broker's transaction fee. Use Decimal arithmetic for money and reconcile every import to its source control total. Construct customer cohorts using stable customer identifiers so renamed accounts do not imitate retention or attrition. Analyze concentration by both revenue and gross contribution where reliable cost attribution exists. Trace unusual month-end journal entries and post-period credits before accepting apparent growth. The contracted QoE accountant evaluates evidence-supported adjustments; the owner retains responsibility for the bid. Every proposed add-back needs a ledger reference, business rationale, recurrence assessment, and replacement-cost treatment. Removing the seller's pay while ignoring the replacement manager's cost overstates transferable earnings.

Keep financing analysis separate from the earnings bridge. The canonical Conservative case is $750,000 of sales multiplied by 8%, producing $60,000; Base is $1,875,000 multiplied by 13.0%, producing $243,750; Scaled is $3,000,000 multiplied by 18%, producing $540,000. These owner-profit figures are after interest and before principal repayments. Do not subtract interest twice, label these amounts EBITDA, or present them as cash available after all debt service. Build a separate liquidity bridge deducting scheduled principal, required capital expenditure, and working-capital increases, with other cash adjustments shown explicitly. For SBA-backed financing, obtain current lender requirements and the applicable SBA procedures; eligibility, seller-note treatment, equity injection, and standby provisions depend on the transaction and current program rules. Historical SBA datasets cannot establish approval or current indebtedness. For conventional and seller debt, model contractual maturities, amortization, security interests, and covenant definitions from actual documents. Never substitute a generic debt-service ratio for the lender's defined calculation. Counsel and the lender resolve intercreditor terms; the controller maintains the payment calendar and flags the earliest projected cash shortfall.

callout.title: Four pre-flight checks before using the diligence model in a bid
callout.body: Advance the model only when each check has an accountable owner and evidence that another reviewer can reproduce.
items: Entity check: confirm the seller, operating subsidiaries, asset owners, debtor names, and relevant jurisdictions against official records and transaction documents.
Access check: document seller authority, granted accounting and bank scopes, permitted recipients, retention period, and revocation procedure before ingestion.
